title: A systematic evaluation of vision-language models for observational astronomical reasoning tasks
abstract: arXiv:2604.24589v2 Announce Type: replace  Abstract: Vision-language models (VLMs) are increasingly proposed as general-purpose tools for scientific data interpretation, yet their reliability on real astronomical observations across diverse modalities remains untested. We present AstroVLBench, a benchmark of over 4,100 expert-verified instances across five tasks spanning optical imaging, radio interferometry, multi-wavelength photometry, time-domain light curves, and optical spectroscopy. We systematically evaluate six state-of-the-art frontier models and find that performance is strongly modality-dependent and uncorrelated with general benchmark rankings. Mechanistic cross-model ablations reveal three concrete bottlenecks. First, prompt grounding exhibits marked model and task dependence: physical guidance yields more balanced classifications on optical imaging, whereas phenomenological prompts better navigate undersampled time-domain data. translated_title: 视觉语言模型在天文观测推理任务中的系统性评估
translated_abstract: 视觉语言模型（VLMs）日益被提议作为科学数据解释的通用工具，但其在跨多种模态的真实天文观测中的可靠性尚未得到验证。我们提出了AstroVLBench，这是一个包含超过4,100个经专家验证实例的基准，涵盖光学成像、射电干涉测量、多波段测光、时域光变曲线和光学光谱五个任务。我们系统地评估了六个最先进的前沿模型，发现其性能强烈依赖于模态，且与通用基准排名不相关。跨模型的机制性消融实验揭示了三个具体的瓶颈。首先，提示词的锚定表现出显著的模型和任务依赖性：物理引导在光学成像任务上产生更均衡的分类结果，而现象学提示则能更好地处理欠采样的时域数据。其次，呈现一维测量数据……（摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文提出了AstroVLBench基准，利用4,100多个经专家验证的跨五种天文观测模态的实例，系统评估了六个前沿视觉语言模型，发现其天文推理性能强烈依赖模态且与通用基准排名无关，并揭示了提示词锚定依赖性和一维数据处理等具体瓶颈。
en_tdlr: This paper introduces AstroVLBench, a benchmark of over 4,100 expert-verified instances spanning five astronomical observation modalities, and shows through systematic evaluation of six frontier vision-language models that their astronomical reasoning performance is strongly modality-dependent, uncorrelated with general benchmark rankings, and bottlenecked by issues such as prompt grounding and one-dimensional data handling.
